description.text: Watsco, Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively, “Watsco,” the “Company”, or “we,” “us,” or “our”) was incorporated in Florida in 1956 and is the largest distributor of air conditioning, heating and refrigeration equipment and related parts and supplies (“HVAC/R”) in the HVAC/R distribution industry in North America. At December 31, 2025, we operated from 695 locations in 43 U.S. States, Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico with additional market coverage on an export basis to portions of Latin America and the Caribbean, through which we serve more than 130,000 active contractors that service the replacement and new construction markets. Our revenues in HVAC/R distribution have increased from $64.1 million in 1989 to $7.2 billion in 2025, resulting from our strategic acquisition of companies with established market positions and subsequent building of revenues and profit through a combination of additional locations, introduction of new products, expansion with industry Original Equipment Manufacturers (“OEMs”) and vendors, technology innovation, and other initiatives. Our principal executive office is located at 2665 South Bayshore Drive, Suite 901, Miami, Florida 33133, and our telephone number is (305) 714-4100. Our website address on the Internet is www.watsco.com and e-mails may be sent to info@watsco.com. Information contained on, or available through, our website is not incorporated by reference in, or made a part of, this report.

about.description_short: Watsco is the largest distributor in the highly fragmented North American HVAC market. Since entering distribution in 1989, Watsco has achieved a 17% compounded annual total shareholder return through a combination of organic growth and the acquisition of more than 70 market-leading businesses. Watsco maintains a solid balance sheet, enabling sustained investments in growth, including the Company's industry-leading technologies. Today, more than 70,000 contractors and technicians engage digitally, empowering them to adopt and integrate Watsco's tools into their daily operations. The Company is also introducing AI-driven initiatives to leverage its extensive data assets and enrich the customer experience. The Company believes its technology ecosystem represents a durable and widening competitive advantage in its highly fragmented industry.

analysis_md:
# WSO — Watsco, Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-18. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Market cap (est) $11.215B at $295.91 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

## What it is
The largest distributor of air-conditioning, heating and refrigeration (HVAC/R) equipment and related parts in North America: 685+ locations serving 125,000+ contractors and dealers, an estimated high-teens share of a fragmented ~$74B market with ~1,400–2,200 independent distributors (company/industry summaries via search). Demand is mostly residential replacement, which is steadier than new construction. Built by buy-and-build — 70+ acquisitions since entering distribution in 1989, still running (three Sunbelt deals in 2025; Jackson Supply closed 2026-06-01, adding ~$230M of annual sales per the Q2 2026 call summary). E-commerce is +13% in H1 2026 at 37% of trailing sales, and OnCallAir generated $1.9B of GMV (Q2 2026 call summary via search).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $569,613,000; capex $34,550,000; SBC $35,344,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $499,719,000 = $13.19/share** (latest FY OE/share, key_numbers.md)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $272,524,000 for FY2025 — far below the conservative figure because FY2025 absorbed a $233,672,000 net-working-capital build (financials_history.csv) around the A2L refrigerant transition. For this distributor the two definitions routinely disagree by working-capital timing in both directions; the OCF-based conservative series is the usable one, and no single year of either series is a run rate.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share by year (financials_history.csv): $8.43 (2021), $13.59 (2023), $18.87 (2024), $13.19 (2025) — the swing factor is inventory/receivables timing, not earnings power.
- Balance sheet (latest FY, key_numbers.md / financials_history.csv): net debt $45.5M = 0.07x normalized OE; cash $433,283,000; operating lease liabilities $462,876,000 sit outside the engine's net-debt basis and are stated here so they are not mistaken for zero. Debt-light by any measure.
- Capital return is dividends, not buybacks: DPS TTM $12.30 (fundamentals.json), annual dividend raised to $13.20/share (Q2 2026 reporting via search) — roughly three-quarters of the TTM OE/share below and essentially all of the median OE/share. Share count rises instead: diluted shares 37,899,859, share-count CAGR +1.70%/yr (key_numbers.md), a −1.70pp drag already inside the engine's growth blend.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $569,613,000 − prior YTD −$185,090,000 + current YTD −$21,440,000 = **TTM $733,263,000**
- Capex: FY $34,550,000 − prior YTD $14,378,000 + current YTD $15,950,000 = **TTM $36,122,000**
- SBC: FY $35,344,000 − prior YTD $17,612,000 + current YTD $16,711,000 = **TTM $34,443,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **38,079,266**
- **TTM OE total $662,698,000 → base OE/share $17.40** (base_source: ttm_json)

**Caution on that base, stated plainly:** the entire uplift vs the normalized median ($13.59) is one half-year working-capital swing — H1 OCF of −$21,440,000 vs −$185,090,000 a year earlier, i.e. a much smaller seasonal inventory ramp after the company met its inventory-reduction target (field stock down ~$200M, Q2 2026 call summary via search). A working-capital release is a level shift, not recurring earnings, and the income statement is moving the other way: Q2 2026 EPS $4.00 was down 11.5% YoY with operating margin 11.3% vs 13.2% (search results). The TTM base is used per the STALE_FY procedure, but the scenario weights are skewed bear-side (45% on bear-or-worse) for exactly this reason, and the median-base method range is documented under Thoughts.

## Moat: 7/10 — strong, not wide
Justification: largest North American HVAC/R distributor (~685+ locations, 125,000+ contractors, estimated high-teens share of a fragmented $74B market) with scale purchasing power, local availability and a scaling digital ecosystem (e-commerce 37% of sales); ROIC proxy stayed 20–34% over the last five fiscal years and never below 17% in ten, and gross margin expanded from 24.2% (2020) to a record 28.0% (2025) — but it sells other makers' products into a still-fragmented field of ~1,400–2,200 distributors, so the moat is strong, not wide.
- Evidence first (fundamentals.json): **ROIC proxy** (after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash) — 20.1% (2016), 21.1% (2017), 21.3% (2018), 17.2% (2019), 20.8% (2020), 26.1% (2021), 34.0% (2022), 26.3% (2023), 24.0% (2024), 20.3% (2025). Above any plausible cost of capital in every one of ten years, through COVID, the post-COVID surge and the A2L downturn — that is what a 7 sits on. **Gross margin**: 24.2% (2020) → 26.6% → 27.9% → 27.4% → 26.8% → a record 28.0% (2025), with TTM at 27.5% as the 2025 OEM/A2L pricing tailwind normalizes (Q2 2026: 27.5% vs 29.3%).
- FOR: scale — largest HVAC/R distributor in North America, estimated 18–20% share vs ~$3B-revenue next rivals, 685+ locations and 125,000+ contractors; ROIC proxy 20.3–34.0% over FY2021–25 and 17–21% in FY2016–20 — above cost of capital through the whole cycle; pricing power proven — gross margin 24.2% (2020) to record 28.0% (2025) via pricing-optimization technology, expanded even as 2025 volumes fell; digital lock-in — e-commerce +13% in H1 2026 at 37% of trailing sales, OnCallAir $1.9B GMV, tools small distributors cannot match; replacement-driven demand plus a debt-light balance sheet funding 70+ buy-and-build acquisitions since 1989.
- AGAINST: no proprietary product — distributes OEM equipment (Carrier and others); OEM concentration and direct/OEM-channel shifts are a standing hostage risk; the market remains fragmented (~1,400–2,200 distributors), so local availability moats erode branch by branch and price competition is constant in commodity segments; gross margin is only 27–28% and the 2025 record leaned on OEM/A2L pricing actions that reversed in Q2 2026 (27.5% vs 29.3%); housing and consumer-durables cyclicality — FY2025 revenue fell 5% on A2L-transition volume softness and slower homebuilding; share count creeps up ~1.7%/yr with no buyback offset and the dividend absorbs essentially all earnings, leaving little reinvestment cushion.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended start is −1.68% (components, key_numbers.md: revenue CAGR 5y 7.45%, revenue CAGR 3y −0.16%, latest FY revenue YoY −4.98%, OE/share CAGR 2y −1.50%, share-count adjustment −1.70pp). Every blend component straddles the A2L-transition trough — FY2025 revenue fell 5% on lower equipment volumes as the refrigerant changeover and slower homebuilding hit (FY2025 release via search). The recent prints have already turned: Q2 2026 revenue $2.10B, +2.1% YoY, with residential HVAC equipment +5% on units and pricing, and management described organic growth of 4–5% through late July with early-July trends at mid-single digits (Q2 2026 call summaries via search); Jackson Supply adds inorganic growth on top. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.043177 / −0.003177 / +0.036823 / +0.076823 / +0.116823 vs the blended start) to −6 / −2 / **+2** / +6 / +10%. The base start of +2% equals the latest quarter's revenue print and sits deliberately below the July organic prints, because gross margin is normalizing (29.3% → 27.5% in Q2) so OE growth lags sales growth near-term; the super-bull start of +10% is an operating-leverage case (volume recovery plus margin marching toward management's 30% gross-margin target), not a sales forecast, and is weighted only 5%. Probabilities were bear-shifted from the 10/25/30/25/10 defaults to 15/30/30/20/5 because the TTM base capitalizes a working-capital release (see Owner's earnings). OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $295.91.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −6.0% | 0.75 | Housing downturn; TTM working-capital release reverses; margin gives back the A2L gains | $71.94 | 5.13% |
| Bear | 30% | −2.0% | 0.90 | Volume stays soft, gross margin settles at ~27%, OE drifts down from the inflated TTM base | $103.97 | 6.64% |
| Base | 30% | 2.0% | 1.00 | Conventional environment: low-single-digit growth, margin holds near the ~27% baseline | $139.38 | 8.36% |
| Bull | 20% | 6.0% | 1.10 | Replacement demand recovers, digital and buy-and-build add share, margin rebuilds | $185.21 | 10.49% |
| Super bull | 5% | 10.0% | 1.25 | Durable compounder path: volume + pricing + margin toward the 30% target | $254.45 | 13.40% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $133.56 (−54.9% vs price), IV@12% $175.54, IV@10% $222.18, weighted IRR 8.13%, base-case IRR 8.36%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 5.88%, terminal value 17.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.54x, net debt 0.07x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $133.56 · 20% at $95.56 · 25% at $74.43. Even the super-bull IV@15% ($254.45) sits below the $295.91 price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above. The TTM base's working-capital flattery is handled by bear-skewed scenario weights and the documented median-base method range, not by hiding it.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier D at 6.64% vs bull-case tier C at 10.49%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — the final tier is the bear/weighted tier D, and no part of the verdict relies on the bull case.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *range* across defensible bases, and unusually it does not change the verdict: the same moat, probabilities and scenario starts on the normalized median base ($13.59/share) give a weighted IRR of 6.89% and IV@15% of $104.30 (engine run, this pass) vs 8.13% / $133.56 on the TTM base — Tier D either way. The preliminary default-input run printed 6.70% / $101.06, also D. Anyone quoting one number for WSO without its base is hiding the ball, but every ball lands in D at $295.91.
- Quality is not the debate: a decade of 17–34% ROIC proxy, record gross margin earned in a down-volume year, net debt 0.07x normalized OE, OE positive 5/5 years, and a dividend raised to $13.20. This is one of the cleanest distribution franchises in the sweep.
- The debate is purely price: at $295.91 the market is paying ~17x the (working-capital-flattered) TTM OE and ~22x the median OE for a business whose revenue fell 5% last year and whose earnings fell double-digits in the latest quarter. The weighted IV@15% is 55% below the price; the stock would need to fall to ~$134 to clear Andrew's 15% hurdle on the weighted path.
- Watch items: whether the Q2 margin normalization (27.5% vs 29.3%) stabilizes at the ~27% baseline management cites or keeps sliding; whether July's mid-single-digit organic growth holds through the seasonally big Q3; Jackson Supply integration; and the payout — a $13.20 dividend on $12.25 of FY2025 EPS leaves no slack if OE stays at the median level.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.13% on the TTM base; 6.89% on the median base — D on both, sized to the bear end of the D–C tier band)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on franchise quality and the balance sheet; the TTM base's working-capital content and the margin normalization path keep any single IRR figure soft, but the tier is robust across bases)
- One-liner: High-quality compounder, moat 7/10 — but at $295.91 it does not clear 15% on any defensible base (weighted IRR 8.1% on the TTM base, 6.9% on the median base; IV@15% $133.56); it clears 15% only at or below ~$134.
